title: Mission Control: telemetry diagnostics
description: The walking slice's own dashboard. Every panel here is fed by a real captured fact travelling Mission Control's durable path - journal, projection, outbox, exporter, Collector, backend - so an empty panel means that path is broken, not that a fixture was forgotten. Phase 7 owns the six product dashboards; this one stays as the compatibility proof.

options.content:
Each panel below is a **cumulative** total exported by Mission Control's durable projection, not a sample of live process state. A restart continues the same stream rather than resetting it, and a batch drained after an outage carries the timestamps and the app version it was recorded under - so a spike here is activity that actually happened then, not a reconnect.

**Genuine zero vs. no data.** An empty panel means nothing has been exported for the selected range. That is different from a zero value, which means the stream exists and its total has not moved. Check **Telemetry queue health** in Mission Control's own API (`GET /api/telemetry/health`) to tell a stopped export apart from a quiet installation.

panels.title: Daemon starts observed
panels.description: Cumulative count of daemon starts this installation has exported. Denominator: none - this is a census of observed starts, not a rate. Read with last_over_time over the selected range rather than as an instant query: these are cumulative totals written only when something happens, and Prometheus marks a series stale five minutes after its last sample - so a plain instant query blanks this panel on any quiet installation, which reads as a broken export rather than as a quiet week.

panels.title: Startup time, p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of daemon startup duration over the whole retained histogram. Buckets are explicit and declared in the metric catalog, so this is comparable across app versions. Read with last_over_time over the selected range rather than as an instant query: these are cumulative totals written only when something happens, and Prometheus marks a series stale five minutes after its last sample - so a plain instant query blanks this panel on any quiet installation, which reads as a broken export rather than as a quiet week.

panels.title: Daemon starts by launch mode and app version
panels.description: Cumulative series, one per launch mode and app version. A NEW line appearing at an upgrade is correct: a changed service.version is a different OTLP resource and therefore a different stream, which is what stops replayed work being credited to a new release.

panels.title: Export connection probes
panels.description: Synthetic connection probes by destination profile and outcome. A probe sends a real, empty OTLP request and then captures its result through the ordinary durable path, so a row here proves both halves. Read with last_over_time over the selected range rather than as an instant query: these are cumulative totals written only when something happens, and Prometheus marks a series stale five minutes after its last sample - so a plain instant query blanks this panel on any quiet installation, which reads as a broken export rather than as a quiet week.

panels.title: Mission Control traces
panels.description: Every completed operation Mission Control exported, searchable at the time it actually ran. Select a Trace ID to open the trace. Honours the Environment and Installation filters above, like every other panel here: a global filter that silently left one panel unfiltered would make this table the one place where a scoped dashboard still shows another installation's traces. A replayed batch appears at its ORIGINAL timestamp, which is why the default range reaches back 24 hours.
